name: Interview mental maths, set 2
description: Mental maths at interview speed: products, quotients, percents, points, fraction gaps, exact products, sequences, volatility and skipping. Each item keeps its own schedule.

items.prose: After a 25% rise, a share costs £150.
items.question: What did it cost before the rise, in pounds?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. The new price is 1.25 times the old one.

byKey.took-off: You took 25% off £150. The 25% was of the old, lower price.
byKey.minus-25: You took off £25. The rise was 25% of the old price, not £25.

explain.text: The new price is 1.25 times the old. So the old price is 150 ÷ 1.25 = £120. Check: 120 plus 25% of 120 is 120 + 30 = 150.

items.prose: A deposit rate rises from 4% to 6%.
items.question: How big is the rise, in percentage points and in percent?

options.why: You used the points as the percent. Against the old 4%, a 2-point rise is 50%.
You swapped the two names. The points are the plain difference, 6 − 4 = 2.
You measured against the new rate, 6%. A percent change uses the old rate: 2/4 = 50%.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Points are the plain difference; percent compares it with the old rate.

explain.text: The rate moved 6 − 4 = 2 percentage points. Against the old 4%, that is 2/4 = 50%. Points measure the gap, and percent measures it against the start.

items.question: Which pair of fractions is further apart: 3/4 and 5/7, or 4/5 and 7/9?

options.text: 4/5 and 7/9, since its numbers are larger.
options.why: Larger numbers do not mean a larger gap. Both cross products differ by 1, so the smaller product of bottoms wins.

options.text: Neither: both gaps are 1, since each pair of cross products differs by 1.
options.why: The 1 sits over the product of the bottoms: 1/28 against 1/45.
You subtracted the tops and the bottoms separately. Cross-multiply instead: 36 − 35 = 1, over 45.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Cross-multiply each pair and divide by the product of the bottoms.

explain.text: Cross-multiply each pair: 3 × 7 − 5 × 4 = 1 and 4 × 9 − 7 × 5 = 1. Each gap is 1 over the product of the bottoms: 1/28 and 1/45. So 3/4 and 5/7 are further apart.

items.prose: Estimate first, then pick the exact product.
items.question: What is $31.2 \times 19.8$?

options.why: You added 31.2 × 0.2. Since 19.8 is below 20, take it off.
You took off 0.2 × 20 = 4. The piece to remove is 31.2 × 0.2 = 6.24.
You took off 31.2 × 0.4. The number 19.8 is only 0.2 below 20.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Round 19.8 to 20, then correct for the rounding.
Not quite right. Look at the differences between terms.

byKey.same-step: You added the last difference, 7, again. The differences grow by 2: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9.
byKey.fib: You added the two terms before, as in 3, 4, 7, 11, 18. Here 4 + 7 is 11, not 12.
byKey.plus-eight: You grew the difference by 1. The differences 1, 3, 5 and 7 grow by 2 each time.

explain.text: The differences are 1, 3, 5 and 7, the odd numbers. The next is 9, so 19 + 9 = 28. Each term is a square plus 3: 5² + 3 = 28.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Divide each term by the one before.

byKey.add-gap: You added the last gap, 4.5, again. Each term is 1.5 times the last, so the gaps grow too.
byKey.double: You doubled 13.5. The ratio is 6/4 = 1.5, not 2.

explain.text: Each term is 1.5 times the one before: 6/4 = 9/6 = 13.5/9 = 1.5. So the next term is 13.5 × 1.5 = 20.25. Half of 13.5 is 6.75, and 13.5 + 6.75 = 20.25.

items.prose: A share's annual volatility is 24%. Take 256 trading days in a year.
items.question: What is its daily volatility, as a percentage to two significant figures?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Volatility scales with the square root of time.

byKey.no-root: You divided by 256. Volatility grows with the square root of time, so divide by 16.
byKey.calendar: You used 365 calendar days. The question gives 256 trading days.
byKey.times: You multiplied by 16. A day is shorter than a year, so divide.

explain.text: Variance grows in proportion to time, so volatility grows with its square root. A day is 1/256 of the year, and √256 = 16. So the daily volatility is 24% ÷ 16 = 1.5%.

items.prose: A test has 50 questions in 6 minutes and lets you skip and return. Near the end you have 42 seconds left. Five questions remain, which would take you 6, 22, 9, 15 and 7 seconds.
items.question: What is the average pace, and what do you do with the 42 seconds?

options.text: 7.2 s a question; skip only the 22 s one and answer the other four in 37 s.
8.3 s a question; skip only the 22 s one.
options.why: You divided 50 by 6, which is questions per minute. 360 s over 50 questions is 7.2 s each.

options.text: 7.2 s a question; skip both the 22 s and the 15 s ones, as both are slow.
options.why: After the 22 s one goes, the other four take 37 s and fit. Skip only what does not fit.

options.text: 7.2 s a question; answer them in order and skip none.
options.why: In order, 6 + 22 + 9 = 37 s leaves 5 s. The last two are lost: three answers, not four.

feedback.correct: Correct. Skip only the 22 s question.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Work out the seconds per question, then fit the most questions into 42 s.

explain.text: The pace is 360 s ÷ 50 = 7.2 s a question. All five need 59 s, so one must go. Dropping the 22 s question leaves 6 + 9 + 15 + 7 = 37 s: four answers.
